prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.62
  gal: 0.38
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
The 2024 Conservative manifesto sets out a “secure future” plan built on five pillars: a stronger economy, opportunities for young people, secure borders and defence, stronger communities and public services, and a pragmatic path to net zero.

Economy and tax
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027 and abolish the main rate of self‑employed NI by the end of the Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT rates.
- “Triple Lock Plus” so both the State Pension and pensioner tax‑free allowance rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%.
- 30 hours’ free childcare from 9 months to school start; reform Child Benefit to a household test with tapering between £120k–£160k.
- Keep to fiscal rules; reduce debt; expand export and trade deals; maintain corporation tax; extend “full expensing” to leasing when affordable.
- 10‑point SME plan (rates support, VAT threshold smoothing, prompt payment enforcement, access to finance, retained growth incentives).
- £36bn redirected from HS2 phase 2 into local transport; nationwide gigabit and standalone 5G; planning and judicial review reforms to speed infrastructure.

Innovation, regulation and government reform
- Public R&D to £22bn; AI compute investment; Advanced Manufacturing Plan; support auto, aerospace, life sciences.
- Regulatory reform using Brexit freedoms; halve spend on consultants; return civil service to pre‑pandemic size; expand digital/AI capability.

Welfare, families and education
- Reform disability benefits and assessments; tighten work capability rules; overhaul fit notes; tougher sanctions; fraud bill; complete Universal Credit rollout.
- Family Hubs in every local authority; expand childcare and wraparound care.
- Mandatory National Service at 18 (competitive paid military/cyber year or civic service one weekend a month).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑value degree courses; create the Advanced British Standard; ban mobiles in school; strengthen parental rights on RSHE; expand SEND places.

Health and social care
- NHS funding rises above inflation; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn tech plan (NHS App as front door, AI diagnostics, data platform); dental recovery plan with NHS service requirement for new dentists; women’s health strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; implement Cass Review.

Borders, immigration and defence
- Monthly Rwanda removals to deter illegal migration; rewrite asylum treaties; legal annual cap on work/family migration that falls each year; higher visa fees and health checks.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; accelerate innovation; sustained support for Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and guarantees.

Crime and justice
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; facial recognition; tougher sentences (including whole‑life terms for more heinous murders), domestic abuse measures; build four new prisons; increase removals of foreign offenders.

Energy, net zero and environment
- Annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants as backup; treble offshore wind; two SMR fleets approved within 100 days; CCS clusters; Wylfa project; keep bills down (no new green levies, no road pricing or frequent flyer levy); national energy‑efficiency vouchers.
- Protect best agricultural land from solar; no fracking; reform water sector oversight; expand nature access and tree/peat programmes; moratorium on deep‑sea mining.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes; fast‑track brownfield; lift London densities; urban development corporations; permanent FTB Stamp Duty relief; new Help to Buy; renters’ reform (end Section 21 after court changes); complete leasehold reform; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- Levelling up funds, towns endowments and community ownership; Backing Drivers Bill (ban local road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, referendums on 20mph/LTNs); £2 bus fare extended for the Parliament; rail reform via Great British Railways.

Society, culture and the Union
- Clarify in law that sex means biological sex in the Equality Act; single‑sex spaces protected; school guidance on gender.
- Support creative industries and grassroots sport; review night‑time economy; protect free speech.
- Strengthen the Union, internal market and direct UK investment across Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; implement Windsor Framework and legacy arrangements.

TEXT_A:
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision
- Tackle the cost-of-living and climate crises together: a faster, fairer transition to a zero‑carbon economy, strong public services, and reduced inequality funded by taxing wealth and pollution.

Health and Care
- NHS: End privatisation; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry; pay restoration; cut waiting lists. Extra funding: £8bn in year one, rising to £28bn by 2030; £20bn capital over five years; primary care uplift and diagnostics expansion; new cancer plan; mental health therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school; assisted dying with safeguards; end new HIV cases by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/year; fair pay and career paths for carers; “Gloria’s Law” for essential care supporters; disability benefits +5% and reform; £3bn to improve children’s social care.

Homes and Planning
- Build 150,000 new social homes/year; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions.
- Green homes guarantee: £29bn insulation for homes, £9bn low‑carbon heat, £4bn to upgrade public buildings, £7bn to adapt to heat; Passivhaus‑level standards for new builds; protect green spaces and Green Belt; empower councils on planning and empty homes.

Energy and Climate
- No new oil and gas; end fossil subsidies; carbon tax rising toward £500/t within a decade.
- Renewables: wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; targets of 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar by 2035; end onshore wind ban; community ownership in new projects.
- Expand grid, storage, interconnectors; support green hydrogen; oppose new nuclear and phase out existing.

Economy and Tax
- Green investment: average £40bn/year (rail, retrofits, energy, water, industry, active travel).
- Public ownership of rail, water, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Fair taxes: wealth tax (1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NI upper limit; reform inheritance and pension reliefs; property tax reform toward land value; windfall taxes; VAT shifts; clamp down on avoidance; borrow to invest.

Work and Welfare
- Repeal anti‑union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; £15 minimum wage; day‑one rights; 10:1 pay ratio cap; protect gig workers; move toward a four‑day week.
- Raise Universal Credit/legacy benefits by £40/week; end five‑week wait; scrap two‑child cap and bedroom tax; disability benefits +5%; uprate pensions; higher Carer’s Allowance; long‑term Universal Basic Income ambition.

Nature, Animals, Food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; nationalise water; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam; rewet peat, expand woodland; £3bn/year for nature restoration; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports, badger cull, factory‑farming cruelties; phase out animal testing.
- Triple farm support; agroecology; reduce pesticides; expand UK horticulture; universal free school meals and breakfast clubs; local food partnerships; cut waste.

Education
- +£8bn for schools and +£2.5bn/year for safe buildings; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; SEND +£5bn; restore school nurses and counsellors.
- FE/skills: £12bn; restore EMA. HE: scrap tuition fees; restore grants; address pension pressures.

Transport
- Public transport first: subsidies to £10bn/year; £19bn/5 years for PT and active travel; renationalise rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/year for cycleways/footpaths.
- Oppose new roads; road pricing; rapid EV transition with scrappage up to £5bn/year; end new ICE sales by 2027, phase out by 2035; 20mph default in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: frequent‑flyer levy; no airport expansion; ban domestic flights under 3‑hour rail alternatives.

Democracy, Rights, Migration
- Fair Politics Act: scrap voter ID; proportional representation; clean party funding; stronger lobbying and media transparency; replace Lords; votes at 16; defend HRA/ECHR; trans self‑ID.
- Migration: end hostile environment, NRPF and 10‑year route; safe asylum routes; right to work; simplify/at‑cost visas; end spousal income rules; voting rights for visa holders.

Culture, Digital, Justice, World
- £5bn for community arts/sport; VAT relief on culture; media ownership caps; complete Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation and creator IP protection.
- Policing: rebuild trust; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; misogyny as hate crime; decriminalise sex work; restorative justice; presumption against short prison terms; +£11bn for MoJ and legal aid.
- Foreign policy: uphold international law; support Ukraine; ceasefire and rights‑based solution in Israel‑Palestine; halt UK arms to Israel; increase aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% by 2033; path to rejoin EU (customs union first, free movement, Erasmus); sign UN nuclear ban, cancel Trident; reform NATO with no‑first‑use.

Judge whether A or B aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "A" | "B"
}
